import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/** Bounded, oldest-to-newest activity history. */
public final class ActivityHistory {
    private final int capacity;
    private final Deque<ActivityEvent> events = new ArrayDeque<>();

    public ActivityHistory(int capacity) {
        if (capacity < 1 || capacity > 256) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity must be between 1 and 256");
        }
        this.capacity = capacity;
    }

    public synchronized void append(ActivityEvent event) {
        events.addLast(Objects.requireNonNull(event, "event"));
        while (events.size() > capacity) {
            events.removeFirst();
        }
    }

    public synchronized List<ActivityEvent> recent() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(events));
    }

    public synchronized int size() {
        return events.size();
    }

    public synchronized void clear() {
        events.clear();
    }
}

interface_contracts.name: activity-history-window
interface_contracts.contract: In dev.atmcompanion.activity, expose public record ActivityWindow(List<ActivityEvent> events, ActivitySummary summary) and public ActivityWindow ActivityHistory.between(Instant startInclusive, Instant endExclusive). The record defensively copies its event list and exposes an unmodifiable list. between returns only currently retained events whose timestamps are >= startInclusive and < endExclusive, preserving append order, with ActivitySummary describing exactly those events using existing summary semantics. Equal endpoints return an empty window with an empty-event summary. Either null endpoint or startInclusive > endExclusive throws IllegalArgumentException. Querying does not modify history, and later history changes do not change a returned window.

acceptance: ActivityWindow provides immutable events and summary components.
between selects only retained events within the inclusive-start, exclusive-end interval and preserves append order even when timestamps are out of order.
Every returned summary describes exactly its returned events, including empty windows.
Equal endpoints yield an empty window; null endpoints and reversed endpoints throw IllegalArgumentException.
Queries leave history unchanged, and returned windows remain stable after subsequent history changes.
Regression coverage exercises the new behavior alongside existing ActivityHistory behavior.

tests: Cover inclusive start, exclusive end, interior and exterior events, equal endpoints, and empty history.
Cover each null endpoint and reversed endpoints expecting IllegalArgumentException.
Cover out-of-order timestamps while asserting append order and exclusion of events no longer retained.
Assert summary accuracy for selected events and empty selections.
Assert history is unchanged by queries, returned windows survive later history changes, and record event lists resist both accessor mutation and mutation through the original constructor list.
